question: Acceptability of a mortgage on landed property as collateral shall be limited to property situated in which locations?

options.A: Only property owned by the obligor for more than 20 years
options.B: Highly industrialized/commercialized areas or high-value residential areas
options.C: Any location whatsoever, provided the title is registered
options.D: Only property located within Federal Capital Territory

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Confirmed verbatim against section 7.7.2.3.1.
community_answer: B. Highly industrialized/commercialized areas or high-value residential areas

question: For a mortgage on landed property, the Expected Forced Sale Value (EFSV) must be adequate to cover what minimum threshold?

options.A: 120% of the loan, plus 12 months' interest
options.D: 80% of the loan only

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed verbatim against section 7.7.2.3.1.
community_answer: A. 120% of the loan, plus 12 months' interest

question: Landed property with less than how many years of remaining ground lease shall NOT be acceptable as collateral?

options.D: 15 years

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Confirmed verbatim against section 7.7.2.3.1.

question: Which of the following is also listed as unacceptable landed property collateral?

options.A: Any property valued below N100 million
options.B: Any property located outside Lagos State
options.C: An uncompleted building, or a country home in a rural area
options.D: Any property with a Certificate of Occupancy under 30 years old

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Confirmed against section 7.7.2.3.1.
community_answer: C. An uncompleted building, or a country home in a rural area

question: Can life assurance policies stand alone as security for a credit facility?

options.A: Left entirely to the discretion of the Relationship Manager
options.B: No, they must be additional to some other tangible collateral
options.C: Yes, always sufficient as sole security
options.D: Yes, but only for facilities below N1 million

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Confirmed verbatim against section 7.7.2.3.5.
community_answer: B. No, they must be additional to some other tangible collateral

question: Acceptability of life assurance policies as credit collateral is limited to which type of credit?

options.A: Personal credits, such as mortgages and personal loans
options.B: Corporate credits exceeding N1 billion only
options.D: Trade finance facilities only

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed verbatim against section 7.7.2.3.5.
community_answer: A. Personal credits, such as mortgages and personal loans

question: Does Access Bank vet the insurance companies whose life assurance policies it will accept as collateral?

options.A: No, any registered insurer's policy is automatically acceptable
options.B: Done once, at the Bank's founding, and never repeated
options.C: Outsourced entirely to the customer's own broker
options.D: Yes, via an annual due-diligence list of acceptable insurers

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Confirmed verbatim against section 7.7.2.3.5.
community_answer: D. Yes, via an annual due-diligence list of acceptable insurers

question: May the collateral currency for cash-collateralized lending be any convertible currency, or must it be local currency only?

options.A: It must be in US Dollars only
options.B: Collateral currency is not addressed by the CPG
options.C: It could be any convertible currency
options.D: It must be in local currency (Naira) only, with no exceptions

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Consistent with the CPG's general cash-collateral provisions.
community_answer: C. It could be any convertible currency

question: Must collateral held by the Bank be revalued periodically, and if so, why?

options.A: Only if the customer requests it
options.B: Yes, since values fluctuate and coverage must stay adequate
options.C: No, the drawdown valuation stays valid forever
options.D: Only real estate needs revaluation

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Consistent with the CPG's collateral monitoring principles.
community_answer: B. Yes, since values fluctuate and coverage must stay adequate

question: In the event of non-compliance with collateralization conditions on a facility, whose responsibility is it to report this?

options.A: The Relationship Manager / Originating Officer responsible for the facility
options.B: Solely the customer's own external auditors
options.C: The Central Bank of Nigeria, as first responder
options.D: No reporting obligation exists once the facility has been disbursed

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Consistent with the CPG's broader principle that the Relationship Manager bears responsibility for the integrity of the credit process.
community_answer: A. The Relationship Manager / Originating Officer responsible for the facility

question: Is careful consideration of collateral adequacy required in every situation, without exception?

options.D: Yes, always, as sound credit practice

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Consistent with the CPG's overall collateral governance framework.
community_answer: D. Yes, always, as sound credit practice

question: For obligors to whom the Bank has extended credit, is there typically a single approval, or several approvals across the Bank, involved in problem recognition, classification of problem exposure, and remedial action?

options.A: No approval is needed once a facility becomes delinquent
options.B: Only the Board of Directors is involved, with no other layer
options.C: Several distinct approvals — for recognition, classification and remedial action
options.D: A single blanket approval covers all three steps together

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Reinforces the delinquency/remedial framework already confirmed in Module 6.
community_answer: C. Several distinct approvals — for recognition, classification and remedial action

question: All Cash, Immaterial and Passive Risk Rating Limit exceptions require approval from the Managing Director and the Head of Credit Risk Management
discussion: Selected Answer: B. False – they require Line ED and CRO, not MD and Head of CRM.

question: Risk Rating Limits are established by the Head of Credit Risk Management and approved by the Criticized Assets Committee
discussion: Selected Answer: B. False – they are established by CRO and approved by MCC, not CAC.

question: Under Access Bank's agricultural financing policy, start-ups and businesses in the first cycle of their operations shall not be considered for funding.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. CPG §10.3.3: Excluded Projects, confirmed verbatim.

question: For the purposes of applying Risk Rating Limits, is a single, uniform method used to determine which obligor risk rating governs, regardless of entity type?

options.C: No, it depends on entity type
options.D: Yes, one method fits every entity

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Reinforces Module 3's Q81.
community_answer: C. No, it depends on entity type

question: Any increases to Total Facilities, whether caused by new facilities or increases to existing facilities, must be approved based on the new Total Facilities amount, per the Credit Facility Approval Grid
discussion: Selected Answer: A. Consistent with the Credit Facility Approval Grid's general re-approval principle.

question: Recommendation and approval of facilities shall be by a minimum of how many Credit Officers, at least one of whom must have the authority to approve the recommended amount?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. Confirmed against the CPG's approval process requirement.

question: An approval may be given by a designee other than the primary named approval authority
discussion: Selected Answer: A. Consistent with the CPG's repeated use of '(or their designees)' language.

question: Discussions and negotiation in respect of repayment or waiver terms on a lost exposure are the responsibility of which unit?

options.C: The Remedial Asset Unit of Credit Risk Management
options.D: The original Relationship Manager, acting entirely alone

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Reinforces Module 6's Q175.
community_answer: C. The Remedial Asset Unit of Credit Risk Management

question: The release of collateral, guarantees or support for any type of credit transaction requires confirmation of what, before release?

options.B: Full repayment and liquidation of the exposure
options.D: A fresh valuation, repayment status aside

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Reinforces Module 2's Q59.
community_answer: B. Full repayment and liquidation of the exposure

question: Adequate security shall be taken for temporary overdrafts not supported by confirmed drafts. Is this a correct statement of policy?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. Consistent with the CPG's overdraft/TOD security expectations.

question: Normally, the maximum tenor for a warehouse financing facility is 12 months. Does the CPG allow this to vary depending on the nature of the goods financed?

options.A: No, 12 months is an absolute ceiling in every case
options.B: No maximum tenor applies to warehouse financing at all
options.C: The maximum is always exactly 6 months, regardless of goods type
options.D: Yes, it may flex with the nature of goods and stock cycle

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Reinforces Module 4's Q124 with additional nuance.
community_answer: D. Yes, it may flex with the nature of goods and stock cycle

question: To qualify for Agricultural financing, a customer should generally have operated an account with the Bank for at least how long?

options.D: 24 months

discussion: Selected Answer: B. CPG §10.3.1: Loan Administration and Disbursement, confirmed verbatim.

question: When the Bank finances the acquisition of heavy equipment and machinery under Agricultural financing, disbursement shall be made directly to the vendors upon presentation of relevant invoices.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. CPG §10.3.1: Loan Administration and Disbursement, confirmed verbatim.

question: Under the Bank's agricultural financing guidelines, moratoriums should generally be limited to principal repayments alone.
discussion: Selected Answer: A. CPG §10.3.1: Loan Administration and Disbursement, confirmed verbatim.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical risk associated with Real Estate Project Finance?

options.D: Environmental Risk

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Clearing Risk is a type of credit risk related to payment systems and is not a specific risk associated with Real Estate Project Finance. Construction, Compliance, and Environmental Risks are typical (section 10.7.5).

question: For Real Estate Finance projects, the Bank will NOT finance:

options.D: Construction costs

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Access Bank will not finance the cost of land, professional and other fees. Lending shall be used entirely to finance construction cost components (section 10.7.11).

question: What is the minimum equity contribution for a Real Estate Finance project?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. The borrower must have equity in the project of not less than 30% of the total cost, including land (section 10.7.11).

question: What is the maximum loan tenor for direct loans to developers for financing housing estates (including any moratorium period)?

options.D: 7 years

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Direct loans to developers for financing housing estates will be for a period or tenor not exceeding five years (including any moratorium period) (section 10.7.16).

question: In Project Finance, the primary source of loan repayment is:

options.B: The revenues generated by the project itself
options.D: A government bailout

discussion: Selected Answer: B. In project finance, the lender looks primarily to the revenues generated by a single project, both as the source of repayment and as security for the exposure (section 10.4).
community_answer: B. The revenues generated by the project itself

question: Which type of risk is mitigated by a fixed‑price, fixed‑delivery Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract in Project Finance?

options.D: Market risk

discussion: Selected Answer: A. A General Constructor Agreement (or EPC contract) that provides a fixed price and a fixed delivery term is a key mitigant for Construction Risk (section 10.4).
community_answer: A. Construction risk, cost and delay

question: What is the minimum sponsor equity contribution required for a Project Finance loan?
discussion: Selected Answer: D. The Sponsor has to ensure a minimum contribution of 20% to the project (section 10.4).

question: In Project Finance, what is the purpose of a Debt Service Reserve Account (DSRA)?

options.D: To pay operating expenses

discussion: Selected Answer: C. A DSRA is built up to ensure debt service payments can be made even if project cash flows are insufficient (section 10.4).
community_answer: C. To reserve against debt-service shortfalls

question: Which of the following is a typical security for Project Finance loans?

options.B: Personal guarantee of the project manager
options.C: Letter of comfort from the government
options.D: A verbal undertaking from the sponsor

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Project finance security includes assignment of operating revenues, mortgage on project facilities, pledge of bank accounts, etc. (section 10.4).

question: In Object Finance, which of the following is a major risk that must be mitigated?

options.D: Performance Risk (the object may not perform as expected)

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Major risks in Object Finance include Performance Risk, Repayment Risk, Diversion Risk, and Tenor Mismatch (section 10.6.3).

question: For Object Finance, what is the minimum equity contribution required from the customer?
discussion: Selected Answer: C. Customer shall make an equity contribution of 10% to 30% depending on the risk profile of the obligor and the transaction (section 10.6.2).

question: In Object Finance, a Marine surveyor report from an Access Bank approved Marine Surveyor shall be obtained as condition precedent to:

options.A: review/analysis for vessels that are brand new
options.B: Drawdown for vessels that are not brand new
options.C: review/analysis for vessels that are not brand new
options.D: Drawdown for vessels that are brand new

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Marine surveyor report from Access Bank approved Marine Surveyor shall be obtained as condition precedent to review/analysis for vessels that are not brand new (section 10.6.2).
community_answer: C. review/analysis for vessels that are not brand new

question: Under Object Finance, the Marine Survey report must state the following, EXCEPT:

options.B: the date for the next special survey
options.C: the date for the next dry docking
options.D: Forced Sale Value of the vessel

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The Marine Survey report must state the market value of the vessel, the date for the next special survey, and the date for the next dry docking. Forced Sale Value is not required (section 10.6.2).
community_answer: D. Forced Sale Value of the vessel

question: In Object Finance, the customer must have a minimum of how many years of proven experience in the type of contract to be undertaken?

options.D: 3 years

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Customer must have minimum of 5 years of proven experience in the type of contract to be undertaken (section 10.6.2).

question: In Object Finance, can a second‑hand vessel be financed if it is free from encumbrance and fit for purpose?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. Second hand vessel can be financed if it is free from encumbrance and fit for purpose (section 10.6.2).

question: In Reserve Based Lending (RBL), which type of reserves does the Bank primarily lend against?

options.D: Undeveloped reserves without any production history

discussion: Selected Answer: C. The lending shall be restricted to Proven, Developed, and Producing (PDP) reserves (section 10.5).
community_answer: C. Proven, Developed, and Producing (PDP) reserves

question: In Reserve Based Lending, the borrowing base is determined by:

options.B: Technical valuation of the borrower's proved reserves
options.D: The Bank's internal risk rating

discussion: Selected Answer: B. The borrowing base is determined by analysing previous production reports and independent engineering evaluations of proved reserves (section 10.5).
community_answer: B. Technical valuation of the borrower's proved reserves

question: In Reserve Based Lending, what is the purpose of a Competent Persons Report (CPR)?

options.A: To assess the borrower's management team
options.B: To confirm the borrower's tax status
options.C: To evaluate the political risk in the host country
options.D: To provide an independent reserve valuation

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The Competent Persons report (CPR) shall contain sufficient information and documentation to support the assumptions and the analysis used to derive the forecasted cash flows and discounted PV (section 10.5).
community_answer: D. To provide an independent reserve valuation

question: In Reserve Based Lending, how often is the borrowing base normally reset?

options.B: Only at the inception of the loan
options.D: Every 6 months

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The borrowing base is normally reset every six months (section 10.5).

question: In Reserve Based Lending, the Bank shall require an independent reserve audit every:

options.D: 4 years

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The revaluation of the reserves shall require an independent reserve audit company to prepare or audit the reserve reports and shall be conducted every 4 years from the date of first availment (section 10.5).

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of Reserve Based Lending (RBL)?

options.A: Secured by liens on oil/gas interests
options.D: Only for retail customers

discussion: Selected Answer: A. RBLs take the form of a borrowing base revolving credit facility secured by liens on oil and gas mineral interests (section 10.5).
community_answer: A. Secured by liens on oil/gas interests

question: In Reserve Based Lending, how is the borrowing base deficiency typically cured?

options.B: The bank simply calling the loan
options.D: Adding more reserves to the collateral base

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The borrowing base deficiency shall be cured by the borrower adding additional oil and gas properties to the collateral base, or by monthly commitment reductions (section 10.5).
community_answer: D. Adding more reserves to the collateral base

question: Under the Mining lending framework, which team acts as the Centre of Excellence for coordinating lending activities to Mining companies?

options.C: The Corporate Banking team in South Africa
options.D: The Head Office Credit Risk Management team

discussion: Selected Answer: C. The Corporate Banking team in South Africa will act as the Center of Excellence, responsible for coordinating the lending activities to Mining companies (section 10.10).
community_answer: C. The Corporate Banking team in South Africa

question: For a Mining transaction, what must be in place before any lending is considered?

options.C: A personal guarantee from the mining engineer
options.D: A letter of comfort from the host government

discussion: Selected Answer: B. Mining Permit must be in place (section 10.8).

question: Which of the following is an example of a government‑sponsored agricultural financing scheme mentioned in the CPG?

options.D: All of the above

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The CPG mentions CACS, ABP, AADS, Rice Distributors' Facility, Export Facilitation Initiative, etc. (section 10.3.5).

question: What is the maximum loan limit under the Commercial Agricultural Credit Scheme (CACS)?

options.D: N1 billion

discussion: Selected Answer: A. The SOL for CACS is set at N2 billion per project (section 10.3.5.1).

question: What is the all‑in interest rate for loans under the Anchor Borrowers' Programme (ABP)?
discussion: Selected Answer: A. Loans under the Anchor Borrowers' Programme are disbursed at an all‑in interest rate of 9% (section 10.3.5).

question: Which of the following is an excluded project under the Agricultural Finance Policy?

options.A: A project to finance an agro‑processing plant
options.C: A project proposed by an unprofitable company
options.D: A project to finance the purchase of agricultural equipment

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Projects proposed by loss‑making or unprofitable companies are excluded (section 10.3.3).
community_answer: C. A project proposed by an unprofitable company

question: For Agricultural financing, what is the target market segment?

options.D: Government-owned projects only

discussion: Selected Answer: A. The target market includes these value chain activities (section 10.3.2).
community_answer: A. Producers, processors, aggregators, exporters, mechanization

question: In Project Finance, what is the purpose of a ‘Preferred Creditor Status’ protection?

options.A: To mitigate transfer and convertibility risk
options.C: To bypass the Environmental Impact Assessment
options.D: To obtain preferential treatment in case of country default

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Multilateral development banks (i.e. IFC, AfDB) “Preferred Creditor Status” protection mitigates transfer and convertibility risk for B Loan participants (section 10.4).
community_answer: A. To mitigate transfer and convertibility risk

question: In Project Finance, what is the typical maximum moratorium period?

options.D: 1 year

discussion: Selected Answer: A. Under the RSSF scheme, moratorium period is 2 years; generally project finance moratoriums are set based on project gestation, not fixed, but often up to 2 years (section 10.4).

question: In Object Finance, the Bank shall ensure that the expiration of the certificate of class is at least:

options.D: 36 months

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Only vessels that are in class shall be financed. The bank shall ensure that the expiration of the certificate of class is at least 24 months (section 10.6.2).

question: In Object Finance, the customer's contract must be a multi‑year time charter agreement – what is the preferred alternative if only a Letter of Intent (LOI) is available?

options.A: Funding still possible with strong 6-month contract assurance
options.D: An LOI works only for government charters

discussion: Selected Answer: A. The use of LOI is strongly discouraged, but the bank shall consider funding on a case‑by‑case basis where there is strong assurance of a firm contract within 6 months (section 10.6.2).
community_answer: A. Funding still possible with strong 6-month contract assurance

question: In Object Finance, what is the purpose of a Performance Bond (PB) from the ship builder (for new vessels)?

options.D: To mitigate performance risk

discussion: Selected Answer: C. Performance Bond is a risk mitigant for performance, delivery, and collateral (section 10.6.3).

question: In Object Finance, what is the maximum loan amount to one obligor (or group) as a percentage of the Bank's total shareholders' funds?
discussion: Selected Answer: D. Financing of objects from one obligor (or a group of related obligors) shall not be more than 20% of the Bank's total shareholders’ funds (section 10.6.11).

question: In Object Finance, the borrower must have a minimum of what percentage equity in the object's cost?
discussion: Selected Answer: B. The borrower must have minimum of 10% equity in the object’s cost (section 10.6.11).

question: In Real Estate Finance, which of the following is NOT a stage of risk associated with Real Estate Project Finance?

options.D: Syndication

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The risks are associated with scheme design, construction, and operation stages; syndication is a funding method, not a risk stage (section 10.7.5).

question: In Real Estate Finance, the Bank shall not fund projects where the borrower is also the contractor, except under what condition?

options.A: Never, even if the borrower is a developer
options.C: Only if the project is below N1 billion
options.D: For an established developer, with one-up approval

discussion: Selected Answer: D. The bank shall not fund projects where the borrower is also the contractor except where the borrower is an established real estate developer (exception to this shall require one up approval) (section 10.7.13).
community_answer: D. For an established developer, with one-up approval

question: In Real Estate Finance, what is the maximum loan tenor for short‑term facilities?

options.D: 2 years

discussion: Selected Answer: D. Short‑term facilities shall be for periods not exceeding 2 years (section 10.7.16).
